summary: Obfuscated install-time dropper via preinstall and binding.gyp
details: Package @7nohe/openapi-react-query-codegen@2.2.2 ships two install-time execution triggers that run an obfuscated payload unrelated to the package's declared purpose (an OpenAPI React Query code generator). package.json declares `"preinstall": "node 3FWCvzduYZg.js"`, and 3FWCvzduYZg.js consists of a single `Function(...)()` invocation over a ~1.6 MB XOR-encoded (key 77) charcode array — the executed code is not shipped as readable source. binding.gyp additionally embeds a GYP `conditions` expression using a Python subclass sandbox escape (`().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()` → `catch_warnings` → `__builtins__['__import__']('os').system(...)`) with unicode-escaped strings that resolve to `os.system('node 3FWCvzduYZg.js')`, causing the same dropper to execute during node-gyp configure. The redundant trigger via binding.gyp survives `--ignore-scripts`. The layered obfuscation (charcode+XOR in JS, unicode-escape + subclass-escape in GYP) has no legitimate purpose for a codegen library and functions to conceal the payload from casual inspection. Installing the package causes attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
